newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Levy to meet King Hussein in Amman.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy to meet King Hussein in Amman.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will travel to Jordan on Tuesday for talks with King Hussein on the Middle East peace process, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Monday.

"On the agenda is a briefing for the king on the peace process, on Levy's meetings with (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat and (PLO negotiator) Nabil Shaath and on the general situation in the Middle East," spokesman Aviv Shir-On said.
Levy met Arafat in Brussels last week and was due to hold talks with Shaath in Jerusalem later on Monday.

Israeli-Palestinian peace moves have been in crisis since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem on land Israel occupied from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war.
"There are also bilateral trade issues and the issue of the joint airport in Aqaba," Shir-On said.
Levy was due to depart for Amman at 10 a.m. (0700 GMT) and will first meet Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh before holding talks with Crown Prince Hassan and King Hussein.
Israel and Jordan signed a peace treaty in 1994 but relations have been rocky since Netanyahu ousted Israel's previous dovish government in May 1996 elections.

Jordan's King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab friend, has expressed growing frustration with Netanyahu over stalled Middle East peacemaking and has said he is "despairing" of the situation in the region.
